source: Lioy et al., Environmental Health Perspectives 110 (2002), Table 1
scope: Three protected settled-dust deposits east of the WTC, collected 16-17 September 2001
limitation: Three deposits are not a mass-balanced sample of the towers. The paper did not measure a <100 um bin.

scope: 33 dust samples collected mostly 17-18 September 2001 within about 1 km
direct_result: Individual grains ranged from centimetre fragments to submicron fibres; composition and grain size were heterogeneous.
limitation: Study targeted environmental composition and spectral detection, not total dust mass or a site-wide particle-size mass distribution.

source: McGee et al., Environmental Health Perspectives 111 (2003), local HTML copy in Judy Wood archive
scope: PM2.5 isolated from collected fallen dust
direct_result: Samples were sieved, aerosolized and size-separated before the PM2.5 fraction was analyzed.
limitation: Chemical composition of an isolated PM2.5 fraction is not the natural PM2.5 mass fraction of the collapse material.

source: Harrit et al., Open Chemical Physics Journal 2 (2009)
scope: Red/gray chips extracted from WTC dust samples
direct_result: A hand-separated sample yielded an approximate chip fraction of 0.1% by weight; DSC releases were estimated at 1.5-7.5 kJ/g.
limitation: Glass and concrete fragments were removed by hand; the paper states total WTC dust mass was difficult to ascertain and provides no bulk concrete-fragmentation model.

source: Judy Wood, From Dust to Dirt pages 4 and 6
direct_result: Quotes a rough 1.176 million ton debris figure and describes visually uniform or nano-dust.
limitation: No representative sampling design, thresholded mass distribution, dust-volume integration, or energy/dose model is supplied.

scope: Debris processed or removed from the full WTC site
direct_result: Official figures vary by operational scope: 1.2 million tons processed at Fresh Kills; 1.642-1.8 million tons removed/cleared from Ground Zero.
limitation: Includes other WTC buildings, later demolition and site material; not the initial mass of WTC 1 and WTC 2 and not a dust mass.

source: Cohesive-fracture surface proxy using published plain-concrete fracture energies
direct_result: Converts density, diameter and 100-200 J/m2 fracture-energy sensitivities to kJ/kg.
limitation: Not WTC-specific; beam fracture energy is not a calibrated comminution law and mechanical coupling efficiency is unknown.
